title: Ottomans, Safavids and Mughals
blurb: Three great empires rule from the Balkans to Bengal. Europe discovers the oceans and slowly overtakes them.

events.title: Ain Jalut
events.what: The Mamluks of Egypt stop the Mongols at Ain Jalut, their first real defeat. The Mongol tide turns.

events.title: A caliph in Cairo
events.what: Three years after Baghdad falls, Baybars seats a surviving Abbasid prince as caliph in Cairo. The Mamluks hold the power; the caliphs give it their blessing.
events.tie: The Cairo caliphs lasted until 1517, when the Ottomans took the last of them to Istanbul.

events.title: Rumi
events.what: Rumi dies in Konya. His Masnavi is still the most read poem in the Muslim world.

events.title: Osman's dream
events.what: Staying with the scholar Edebali, Osman dreams that a tree grows from him until its shade covers the world. Edebali reads it as an empire and gives him his daughter in marriage.
events.tie: Ottoman histories tied the dynasty's rise to the blessing of a scholar, not only to the sword.
events.note: The story is told by Ottoman chroniclers more than a century later. It is a founding legend, and its date is unknown.

events.title: A Mongol khan becomes Muslim
events.what: Ghazan, Mongol ruler of Persia, accepts Islam with thousands of his soldiers. Thirty-seven years after Hulagu burned Baghdad, his great-grandson prays toward Makkah.
events.tie: The conquerors were won over by the faith of the conquered: within a few decades most Mongol khans in the west were Muslim.

events.title: Islam in Sumatra
events.what: Sultan Malik al-Salih of Pasai is buried under an Arabic gravestone, the first Muslim king known in Southeast Asia.
events.tie: Islam reached Southeast Asia through traders and teachers, not armies; today Indonesia is home to more Muslims than any other country.

events.title: Osman's state
events.what: Osman founds a small frontier state in Anatolia. It will become the Ottoman empire and last 623 years.
events.tie: In 1453 the Ottomans took Constantinople, a city whose conquest by Muslims the Prophet ﷺ is reported in a hadith to have foretold.

events.title: Islam on the Volga
events.what: Uzbeg Khan makes Islam the faith of the Golden Horde, the Mongol state of the Russian steppe. Its Tatar heirs are the Muslims of Kazan and Crimea today.
events.tie: Russia's Tatar Muslims trace their faith to these khans and to the Volga Bulghars, who accepted Islam four centuries earlier.

events.title: Mansa Musa's Hajj
events.what: Mansa Musa of Mali goes on Hajj with so much gold that prices in Cairo crash. Timbuktu becomes a city of scholars.
events.tie: Hajj is owed to Allah by all who are able (3:97); Mansa Musa's journey made Mali famous and brought scholars and books to Timbuktu.

events.title: Ibn Battuta sets out
events.what: Ibn Battuta leaves Tangier for Hajj and keeps going for 29 years, from Mali to China. The Muslim world is one connected space.

events.title: Bursa, the first capital
events.what: Osman's son Orhan takes Bursa from Byzantium after a long siege and makes it his capital. Osman is buried there. The frontier band now has a city.
events.tie: Bursa's mosques, markets and tombs set the pattern for every Ottoman city to come.

events.title: Kilwa and the Swahili coast
events.what: Ibn Battuta calls Kilwa one of the most beautiful cities in the world. Its Muslim sultans grow rich shipping gold from Zimbabwe across the Indian Ocean.
events.tie: Swahili, the language of the coast, is full of Arabic words carried by Muslim traders and sailors.

events.title: The Black Death
events.what: The Black Death crosses from the Black Sea into Egypt, Syria and Europe. A third of the population dies.
events.tie: The Prophet ﷺ taught that if plague strikes a land you are in, do not leave it, and if it is elsewhere, do not enter it.

events.title: Mamluk Cairo
events.what: Only years after the Black Death, Sultan Hasan begins a vast mosque and college below the Cairo citadel. Mamluk Cairo is the greatest city of the Muslim world.
events.tie: Al-Azhar and Cairo's colleges drew students from Mali to Java, and scholars such as Ibn Hajar taught here.

events.title: Timur's Samarkand
events.what: Timur seizes power in Central Asia and makes Samarkand his capital. He fills it with blue domes raised by craftsmen taken from the cities he sacked.
events.tie: Timur claimed to fight for Islam, yet he sacked Delhi, Baghdad and Damascus; most of the people he killed were Muslims.

events.title: Ibn Khaldun
events.what: Ibn Khaldun writes the Muqaddimah, the first study of how states rise and fall. Sociology and economics begin here.

events.title: Timur
events.what: Timur crushes the Ottomans at Ankara and captures the sultan. The Ottomans recover; Timur's empire does not outlive him.

events.title: Zheng He's fleets
events.what: Zheng He, a Chinese Muslim admiral, sails giant fleets to India, Arabia and East Africa.
events.tie: Zheng He's father had made the Hajj, and Muslims in Indonesia still remember the admiral in mosques named after him.

events.title: Ulugh Beg's observatory
events.what: Timur's grandson Ulugh Beg builds a giant observatory in Samarkand. His tables chart over a thousand stars and measure the year to within a minute.
events.tie: The Quran points to the sun and moon as a way to count the years; Muslim astronomers made that counting a science.
events.note: Ulugh Beg was killed in 1449 on his own son's orders and the observatory was later destroyed. Its great arc was dug up again in 1908.

events.title: Constantinople falls
events.what: Mehmed II, aged 21, takes Constantinople. The Byzantine empire ends after 1,100 years. Hagia Sophia becomes a mosque.

events.title: The printing press
events.what: Gutenberg prints the Bible with movable type in Mainz. Within fifty years Europe has millions of printed books.
events.tie: The first Arabic Quran ever printed came from Venice around 1537, full of errors; Muslims went on copying it by hand for nearly three more centuries.

events.title: Granada surrenders
events.what: Granada surrenders. Muslim Spain ends. Months later Columbus sails west from the same kingdom.
events.tie: The Alhambra still bears the words 'there is no victor but Allah'; Spain's Muslims soon faced forced conversion and, a century later, expulsion.

events.title: The Jews expelled from Spain
events.what: From the Alhambra, Ferdinand and Isabella order every Jew in Spain to convert or leave. Tens of thousands go, and many find refuge in the Ottoman empire.
events.tie: Sultan Bayezid II welcomed them; Thessaloniki and Istanbul became great Jewish cities under Muslim rule.
events.note: The famous line in which Bayezid mocks Ferdinand for making his own land poorer is a later story of uncertain origin.

events.title: Columbus reaches the Americas
events.what: Columbus, sailing for Spain, lands in the Bahamas. Within a century Spain and Portugal rule from Mexico to Brazil.
events.tie: Columbus wrote that he had watched the royal banners raised over the Alhambra that January, the month Muslim Spain ended.

events.title: Europe reaches India
events.what: Portugal reaches India around Africa. European fleets begin to take the Indian Ocean trade from Muslim merchants.
events.tie: Muslim merchants had carried Islam along these sea routes to India, East Africa and Indonesia; now they began losing the trade to European fleets.

events.title: The Safavids
events.what: Shah Ismail founds the Safavid state and makes Shia Islam the religion of Persia.
events.tie: Before the Safavids most Persians were Sunni, and Persia had produced scholars like Imam Muslim of Nishapur; after them Iran became mostly Shia.

events.title: Portugal takes Malacca
events.what: Portugal seizes Malacca, the Muslim port that controlled the sea trade between India and China.
events.tie: Malacca's sultans had spread Islam across the Malay world; after its fall, Muslim traders moved to ports like Aceh and carried the faith further.

events.title: The Piri Reis map
events.what: The Ottoman admiral Piri Reis draws a world map showing the coasts of Africa and the new Americas. Among his sources was a map by Columbus.
events.tie: Found in Topkapi Palace in 1929, it is one of the oldest surviving maps to show the Americas.

events.title: Chaldiran
events.what: Selim I's guns defeat Shah Ismail at Chaldiran. The Sunni Ottomans and the Shia Safavids fight on and off for more than a century.
events.tie: The border they finally fixed at Zuhab in 1639 still roughly divides Turkey and Iraq from Iran.

events.title: The Reformation
events.what: Luther's theses split western Christianity. Printing presses spread the argument; Muslim lands adopt print much later.
events.tie: Muslim lands long preferred hand-copied books, above all the Quran; the first Ottoman press in Arabic script opened in Istanbul only in 1727.

events.title: Ottomans take Egypt and the Hijaz
events.what: Selim I takes Syria, Egypt and the Hijaz. The Ottoman sultan becomes guardian of Makkah and Madinah.
events.tie: The sultans took the title Servant of the Two Holy Sanctuaries and for four centuries sent and guarded the Hajj caravans from Damascus and Cairo.

events.title: Suleiman the Lawgiver
events.what: Suleiman becomes sultan and reigns for 46 years. Europe calls him the Magnificent; his own people call him Kanuni, the Lawgiver.
events.tie: His chief mufti Ebussuud worked to bring the sultan's laws into line with the sharia.

events.title: The fall of Tenochtitlan
events.what: Cortes and his native allies take the Aztec capital after a long siege, helped by smallpox. One of the world's great cities becomes Mexico City.
events.tie: The conquerors came from a Spain fresh from its war on Granada; in their letters they even called the Aztec temples 'mosques'.

events.title: The Mughal Empire
events.what: Babur wins at Panipat and founds the Mughal empire. Under Akbar it holds a quarter of the world's people.
events.tie: The Mughals made India a great centre of Muslim civilisation, from the mosques of Delhi and Lahore to the Hanafi law collection al-Fatawa al-Alamgiriyya.

events.title: Suleiman at Vienna
events.what: Suleiman the Magnificent besieges Vienna. The Ottomans now rule Hungary and the Balkans, and the Mediterranean is theirs.

events.title: The Inca empire falls
events.what: Pizarro captures the Inca emperor Atahualpa at Cajamarca, takes a room full of gold as ransom, then kills him. The Andes fall to Spain.
events.tie: American silver soon flooded the world; historians link it to the inflation that shook Ottoman money in the late 1500s.
events.note: How much American silver caused Ottoman inflation is debated by historians.

events.title: Kazan falls to Russia
events.what: Ivan the Terrible storms Kazan, capital of a Muslim Tatar khanate. Its imam Qol Sharif dies defending the city with his students, and the mosques are pulled down.
events.tie: It was the first Muslim land Russia conquered; a new Qol Sharif mosque opened inside the Kazan kremlin in 2005.

events.title: The first coffee houses
events.what: Two Syrians open Istanbul's first coffee house. Coffee, first drunk by Sufis in Yemen to stay awake for night prayer, spreads to Europe through Ottoman lands.
events.tie: The word coffee comes from the Arabic qahwa, by way of the Turkish kahve.
events.note: Scholars argued for decades over whether coffee was lawful; it was briefly banned in Makkah in 1511 before being accepted.

events.title: Akbar
events.what: Akbar becomes Mughal emperor at thirteen. He rules for half a century and doubles the empire.
events.tie: Akbar's mixing of faiths drew criticism from Sunni scholars like Shaykh Ahmad Sirhindi, whose revival shaped Indian Islam for centuries.

events.title: Sinan's Suleymaniye
events.what: The architect Sinan completes the Suleymaniye mosque. He designs over 300 buildings across the empire.

events.title: Lepanto
events.what: A Christian fleet destroys the Ottoman navy at Lepanto. The Ottomans rebuild within a year but the sea is now contested.

events.title: The fall of Songhai
events.what: A Moroccan army with firearms destroys the Songhai empire at Tondibi. The great age of West African empires ends.

events.title: Isfahan, half the world
events.what: Shah Abbas makes Isfahan his capital and fills it with mosques and squares. Persians call it half the world.
events.tie: Its Shah Mosque and Shaykh Lutfallah Mosque, covered in blue tile and Quranic calligraphy, are among the masterpieces of Islamic architecture.

events.title: Aceh, the Porch of Makkah
events.what: Iskandar Muda becomes sultan of Aceh and makes it the strongest power on the Malacca Strait. Pilgrims from across Southeast Asia sail from here to Makkah.
events.tie: Aceh asked the Ottomans for help against Portugal and received guns and gunners in the 1560s; it is still called the Porch of Makkah.

events.title: The Moriscos expelled
events.what: Spain orders out the Moriscos, descendants of Muslims forced to become Christian. About 300,000 are shipped to North Africa, and nine centuries of Islam in Spain end.
events.tie: Many Moriscos had kept Islam in secret for a century, writing Spanish in Arabic letters, a script called aljamiado.

events.title: The Qing take China
events.what: Manchu armies take Beijing and found the Qing dynasty, which will rule China until 1912.
events.tie: Under the Qing, Chinese Muslim scholars such as Liu Zhi explained Islam in classical Chinese, joining it to Chinese learning.

events.title: The Taj Mahal
events.what: The Taj Mahal is completed in Agra as a tomb for Mumtaz Mahal. Mughal wealth at its peak.
events.tie: Its great gate carries the Quran's call to the soul at peace: 'Enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise' (89:27-30).

events.title: Aurangzeb
events.what: Aurangzeb takes the Mughal throne and rules for half a century, and the empire reaches its largest size. After his death in 1707 it breaks apart.
events.tie: He sponsored the Fatawa-e-Alamgiri, a great book of Hanafi law compiled by hundreds of scholars.
events.note: Many Muslims remember him for his piety and simple life; others remember his wars and harshness. Historians still debate his rule.

events.title: The Hajj caravan
events.what: The traveller Evliya Celebi joins the great caravan that leaves Damascus every year for Makkah. Tens of thousands march for over a month, guarded by the sultan's soldiers.
events.tie: With every caravan the sultans sent the surre, gifts and money for the people of the Two Holy Cities.

events.title: The second siege of Vienna
events.what: The second siege of Vienna fails. The Ottomans begin a slow retreat from Europe that lasts 230 years.

events.title: The first Ottoman press
events.what: Ibrahim Muteferrika prints the first book in Ottoman Turkish, a dictionary. His press prints maps, histories and science, but not the Quran.
events.tie: Printing the Quran was long resisted, out of reverence for the hand-written word and the scribes who wrote it.
events.note: Historians still debate why Muslim lands took up printing so late.

events.title: Muslims in chains
events.what: Ayuba Suleiman Diallo, son of an imam in Senegal, is seized and sold to Maryland. A letter he writes in Arabic wins his freedom; in London he writes out the Quran from memory.
events.tie: Many Africans carried across the Atlantic were Muslims; some, like him, wrote Arabic and kept their prayers in slavery.
events.note: Historians' estimates of how many enslaved Africans were Muslim vary widely.

events.title: The Quran in Persian for India
events.what: In Delhi, Shah Waliullah translates the Quran into Persian, the language of educated Indians, so people can understand it and not only recite it. His sons later put it into Urdu.
events.tie: Deoband and many other South Asian schools trace their teachers back to him.

events.title: The first Saudi state
events.what: A pact between a ruler and a reformer in Diriyah founds the first Saudi state.
events.tie: Ibn Abd al-Wahhab called for a return to pure tawhid; Muslims have argued over his movement and its legacy ever since.

events.title: Plassey
events.what: The British East India Company defeats the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey. The richest Muslim province falls to a trading company.
events.tie: Bengal was home to tens of millions of Muslims; Company rule there began British rule over India's Muslims that lasted almost two centuries.

events.title: The French Revolution
events.what: The French Revolution. Nationalism and the modern state are born, ideas that will reshape Muslim lands too.
events.tie: Ideas of the nation and the secular state spread from France into Muslim lands, later shaping the end of the Ottoman caliphate and new borders.

events.title: Napoleon in Egypt
events.what: Napoleon invades Egypt with an army and a team of scholars. The shock of European power starts the modern Muslim reform debate.
events.tie: Al-Azhar's scholars led Cairo's revolt against the French, and the historian al-Jabarti recorded the occupation day by day.
